mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive monthly observations
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months indicates persistent labor market slack, reducing wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 4.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls by >0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand sectors, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) of 0.75% or more, combined with a concurrent rise in CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 6%, signals aggressive tightening in a high-inflation environment, which increases recession risk and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises by >=0.75% and CPIAUCSL > 6% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by >100,000 for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases by >100,000 for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of fiscal stimulus.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS increases by >5% month-over-month and no major fiscal stimulus is announced.
